newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts Governor Weld announces resignation.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts Governor Weld announces resignation.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld said on Monday he would resign on Tuesday from the office he has held for the past seven years to campaign for the post of U.S. ambassador to Mexico.

Weld, a fiscally conservative but socially liberal Republican, said he would step down at 5 p.m. (2100 GMT) Tuesday to lobby senators for support in the face of stiff opposition from a fellow Republican, Sen. Jesse Helms, the conservative chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee who has the power to block his appointment.

"The confirmation battle in Washington is likely to be a protracted one," Weld told a state house news conference. "I have consequently decided to resign the office of governor effective 5 p.m. tommorrow. I don't believe it would be fair to the people of Massachusetts to permit the conduct of their government to become embroiled in the vagaries of Washington politics."
Helms has said publicly he objects to Weld's views on the medicinal use of marijuana and to his drug prosecution record and has blocked any hearings on the appointment.

Earlier this month, Weld called a news conference to challenge President Bill Clinton to fight for the nomination and said his differences with Helms reflected an ideological rift in the Republican Party.
"In plain language, I am not Senator Helms' kind of Republican," Weld said then.
